beats.hook: I came home to find my best friend of eight years sitting in my apartment — with my boyfriend — and a stack of my bank statements on the table.
beats.the_wrong: She had been borrowing my login to "check her balance." Turns out she'd been transferring small amounts — forty dollars here, sixty there — for almost a year. Eleven hundred dollars total.
beats.the_plan: I didn't confront her. I smiled. I told her I was so glad she was there — because I needed her help planning a surprise.
beats.the_execution: I'd already called the bank. The fraud hold was active. Her name was flagged. When she tried to use the joint account she'd quietly added herself to — the one she thought I didn't know about — her card declined. At the coffee shop. In front of her coworkers. The bank called me to confirm the block. I confirmed it.
beats.the_satisfaction: She texted me four times that afternoon. I read every one. Then I forwarded the transfer history to her mom — who had co-signed her lease. Here's what I still think about: my boyfriend knew. He saw the statements. He said nothing for three weeks. So what would you have done — deal with one betrayal at a time, or blow up both on the same day?
beats.cta: Drop your answer below — and if you want to know what happened with the boyfriend, tell me in the comments and I'll post part two.
